idea: Find the two points that are nearest to each other without comparing every pair. Sort by x and split in the middle. The best pair lies in the left half, in the right half, or across the middle. A crossing pair must be in a thin strip around the middle line, and in the strip, sorted by y, each point only needs checking against the next few points.
useWhen: Collision detection and nearest-neighbour checks in games and maps
Clustering, where the closest two points are merged first
Teaching divide and conquer with a non-obvious combine step
avoidWhen: There are very few points: comparing all pairs is simpler and as fast
The points move all the time: a spatial grid or tree may suit better
